findings.originalRecommendation: Do not set FEE_ENGINE_ADDRESS to the deployed 0x2f1f… engine. Redeploy with two changes. (1) Add a permissionless credit of untracked balances for currencies of verified pools (balanceOf minus tracked amount). Crediting donations is harmless because every outflow goes to burn, the Swapper or Automation. (2) Replace the exact-share equality with share > 0, or at least the expected share. Add fork t

findings.finding: /api/launch/prepare uses one global lock and saves a plan for every anonymous call
findings.originalRecommendation: Replace the global boolean with a small semaphore (for example 4) plus per-IP/per-creator single-flight. Persist plans only after the wallet-side validate/simulate step, or cap unsigned plans per creator per hour and delete unsigned plans after about 1 day.
findings.disposition: Global prepare lock / anonymous plan growth — implemented
findings.implementationAndRemainingAcceptance: Four shared slots, request merge, bounded queue/budgets, compact/protected plan lifecycle.

findings.finding: The stop-signing switch is still read from the isolate's process.env snapshot. Today's production rollout showed that this snapshot does not refresh on a bindings-only release, so the documented way to stop signing is unreliable.
findings.originalRecommendation: - Read every security-relevant runtime value from the native `env` binding (or this.env) on each request instead of process.env at construction time. That covers ENABLE_*_TRANSACTIONS, the treasury, the guard and fee-engine addresses, and the secrets. - Make every release replace the isolate, for example by baking the commit SHA or build id into the Worker bundle as a constant. - Add a workerd sta
findings.implementationAndRemainingAcceptance: Native per-request bindings and independentCAS stop source implemented/tested; DBcontrols installedpaused andlegacy publicflags stopped2026-10-08. Protocol-1 compatible runtime baseline remainspending.

findings.finding: Registration requires live totalSupply == 1B, but any holder can call DopplerERC20V1.burn(), so anyone can permanently block a launch from being listed
findings.originalRecommendation: Bind supply to the creation receipt, not live state: check the mint Transfer(0x0 → …, 1e27) or Create event in the receipt logs, or read totalSupply at blockNumber: receipt.blockNumber (needs archive state, see the related finding). Never compare against live totalSupply when re-verifying already-confirmed launches.
findings.implementationAndRemainingAcceptance: Creation mint/Create/FeeScheduleSet receipt evidence; no current totalSupply requirement.

findings.finding: Anyone can use up the shared LI.FI API key quota, so nobody can launch for up to 2 hours
findings.originalRecommendation: Cache readOpeningValuation per (chain, asset) for part of LAUNCH_PRICE_TTL and share in-flight requests. Validate all quote inputs and run all non-LI.FI checks before any LI.FI call. Add a global LI.FI token bucket in the DO that fails fast before the key runs out. Add a Cloudflare rate-limiting rule on /api/first-buy/* and /api/launch/prepare, and set workers_dev:false so the rule cannot be bypas
findings.implementationAndRemainingAcceptance: Cross-chain durable budgets/circuit, caches, paid-recovery reserve; edge WAF setup pending.

findings.finding: 30-minute TWAP on a thin, single-venue MUSEGOD/WETH pool can be manipulated against an ownerless Swapper, and the observation ring can be cheaply flooded to freeze buybacks
findings.originalRecommendation: Before activating, raise the pool's observation cardinality (increaseObservationCardinalityNext) well above the number of swap-blocks in 30 minutes. Use a longer TWAP or an extra guard that compares spot with the TWAP. Cap how much WETH the Swapper can receive per window (forwarder included). Or keep the forwarder approval at 0 until the pool is deep enough.
findings.implementationAndRemainingAcceptance: Correlated spot/5m/30m check, rolling 0.01 WETH cap; live retained-history/cardinality and market impact review remain canary tasks. No claim of independent price truth.

findings.finding: Priced-asset buyback fees can be locked in the engine forever if a configured feed is deprecated or stays paused; there is no fallback path
findings.originalRecommendation: In the redeployed engine, add a time-locked fallback: after N days of continuous quote failure, allow releaseUnpriced for that asset. Or add a narrowly scoped, time-delayed recovery to the Automation account.
findings.disposition: Retired priced feed strands fees — implemented alternative
findings.implementationAndRemainingAcceptance: Treasury-proposed feed replacement after seven days. Keep priced floor; no unpriced custody fallback.

findings.finding: Locked first buys are now live, but lock status and claim exist only on the registered-token page, so any registration failure strands a 30–365 day lock with no claim path in the app
findings.originalRecommendation: - Decouple lock status and claim from registration: let the client read Bundler.vestingOf and claimable for any asset in the user's local launch history, or for an asset address the user pastes. - Offer claim from TransactionHistory for confirmed launches that carry a lock. - Fix the registration blockers already reported: totalSupply equality and burn griefing, and reads at the receipt block. - D
findings.disposition: Unregistered locks have no claim path — implemented
findings.implementationAndRemainingAcceptance: Chain+token Bundler lookup, history/address entry, independent recipient claim.

findings.finding: On-chain first-buy deadline is the 60-second LI.FI quote expiry, which leaves about 55 seconds for review, approval and signing
findings.originalRecommendation: Separate the guard deadline from the price-snapshot TTL, for example quote time plus 5 minutes, and keep the 60 s freshness gate only for building the preview. Alternatively, re-quote after the approval is mined. Show a visible countdown. Cache the per-block guard verification result (the guard and Bundler code are immutable) so a transient RPC error cannot invalidate a flow that is already in pro
findings.implementationAndRemainingAcceptance: V2 five-minute fixed finalization window; approval refresh preserves floor; old semantics readable.

findings.finding: Client checks server LI.FI timestamps against the local clock with zero tolerance; a clock ~10 s slow makes every preview fail as 'expired'
findings.originalRecommendation: Return serverTime with the plan and validate client-side against a skew-corrected clock. Or keep strict freshness checks server-side (validate/simulate already do this) and on the client only check expiry with a tolerance. Show a clock-skew-specific error.
findings.implementationAndRemainingAcceptance: Server time + quote-specific monotonic anchors.

findings.finding: One global 'preparing' lock plus unauthenticated, persisted ~63 KB prepares lets a single client block all launch previews and grow the database
findings.originalRecommendation: Replace the global boolean with a per-IP/per-creator token bucket and a small bounded queue. Cache the LI.FI opening valuation per asset for a few seconds. Store a compact plan (drop the duplicate copies of calldata in plan.data, transaction.data, prepared.transaction.data and createParams) and expire unsigned plans after minutes, not 30 days.
findings.disposition: Global lock / duplicate persisted calldata — merged with 2
findings.implementationAndRemainingAcceptance: Shared queue/budget and compact protected recovery payload.

findings.finding: Reconcile re-registers every confirmed launch forever, with O(N) RPC and O(N²) DB egress per cycle; rows that fail re-verification permanently fill the 100-row window
findings.originalRecommendation: Take rows out of the active queue once confirmed with enough depth: query status='pending' only, and handle reorgs with a bounded re-check of recently confirmed rows (for example the last N blocks or hours). Look up the token by tx_hash with an indexed query instead of tokens(). Bump updated_at or apply backoff on failure so failing rows rotate. Add cleanup for stale pending and replaced rows.
findings.implementationAndRemainingAcceptance: Indexed hash lookup, pagination/backoff, bounded canonical recent checks and finalization.

findings.finding: A spoofed or compromised LI.FI quote can set any minimum output; nothing checks the quoted output independently
findings.originalRecommendation: Before returning or signing a quote, require USD(expectedOut) to be within a few percent of USD(amountIn - fee). Use cached /token prices fetched separately from the /quote call, and repeat the check client-side with the /first-buy/prices data. If the Robinhood RPC supports it, also simulate with asset-change tracing (eth_simulateV1) and require the account's toToken balance delta >= minimumOut. S
findings.implementationAndRemainingAcceptance: Independent-price/spread warnings; calldata/recipient/amount/route/minimum validation and full simulation stay hard. Source compromise is not declared solved by warnings.

findings.finding: Zero-tolerance client clock checks reject valid server quotes and launch previews when the browser clock is a few seconds slow
findings.originalRecommendation: Allow a bounded skew (e.g. quotedAt/obtainedAt <= now + 30 s) in the client-side checks. Better, have the client compute an offset from a server Date header and pass `now + offset`. Keep the strict checks on the server, which uses its own clock.
findings.implementationAndRemainingAcceptance: Quote anchors and LI.FI's independent validity.

findings.finding: A failure after activation always rolls back automatically; for a stop-signing release, that turns signing back on
findings.originalRecommendation: Do not auto-roll back a candidate that only lowers privileges (signing true→false, guard removed). Instead, mark it "needs attention" and leave it active. Long term, make the kill switch independent of deploys.
findings.implementationAndRemainingAcceptance: Persistent pause, privilege-preserving rollback and protocol compatibility.

findings.finding: No functional smoke test after deploy and no monitoring or alerting; a release that broke LI.FI pricing was marked successful
findings.originalRecommendation: - Add a read-only smoke gate after activation: /api/chains/4663/first-buy/prices, /api/stocks verified count, launchGuard non-null, and a read-only /api/quote. - Set up an external uptime monitor on /readyz and /config that alerts on 503, a writesEnabled change, or launchGuard becoming null. - Add Cloudflare Workers error-rate alerts and a log alert on "Launchpad maintenance failed".
findings.disposition: Missing functional smoke / monitoring — partial external completion
findings.implementationAndRemainingAcceptance: Functional release smoke implemented; sustained external alert/monitor setup and production smoke pending.

findings.finding: No human approval gate: any push to the unprotected master branch goes to 100% of production, with signing on, about 3 minutes later
findings.originalRecommendation: - Add `environment: production` to the release job, with a required reviewer and a deployment-branch policy limited to master. - Move CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN into an environment secret. - Protect master: require a PR with human review and block force-push. - Require 2FA at the org level. - Consider activating the candidate at a small percentage first, then promoting it.
findings.disposition: Manual CI approval proposal — explicitly not implemented
findings.implementationAndRemainingAcceptance: User retains master-push automatic deployment; tests/artifact/smoke checks strengthened. No new manual CI gate.

findings.finding: One global launch-preview lock in a single Durable Object lets one IP block every creator's preview
findings.originalRecommendation: - Replace the global flag with per-creator/IP single-flight plus a small bounded queue. - Add a Cloudflare rate-limit rule for /launch/prepare and /first-buy/quote. - Cache each asset's LI.FI opening reference for its 60-second TTL.
findings.disposition: One client blocks all preview — merged with 2
findings.implementationAndRemainingAcceptance: Four slots and bounded queue; actual production concurrency/latency calibration pending.

findings.finding: The rollback check has no propagation wait, so a successful rollback is reported as "rollback=failed"; the tests mock this path
findings.originalRecommendation: - Reuse verifyProductionCandidate's bounded retry and wait for verifyRollback. - Report "rollback activated, edge propagation pending" separately from "rollback failed". - Add a test where the old header persists for one attempt.
findings.implementationAndRemainingAcceptance: Bounded wait/retry and explicit propagation outcome.

findings.finding: The stop-signing switch does not stick: the next automatic release turns signing back on, and every rollback version also has signing on
findings.originalRecommendation: - Make release.ts refuse to publish when the previous version's effective signing flags (ENABLE_ROBINHOOD_TRANSACTIONS ?? ENABLE_MAINNET_TRANSACTIONS, ENABLE_BASE_TRANSACTIONS) or guard addresses differ from wrangler.jsonc, unless the change is committed in git. - Better: move the kill switch to runtime state that an authenticated operator can toggle without a deploy, such as DO storage or KV. - W

findings.implementationAndRemainingAcceptance: Independent persistent stop state and binding drift checks.

findings.finding: Every 30–90 s the background reconcile job re-registers every confirmed launch forever and downloads the whole token table once per row
findings.originalRecommendation: Only re-check confirmed rows until a finality cutoff (for example 1 hour or the L1-batch-posted block), then exclude them from the reconcile query. Replace tokens().find with a tx_hash lookup (unique index (scope,tx_hash) already exists). Delete 'replaced' rows in musegod_cleanup to match SQLite. Paginate /api/tokens.
findings.implementationAndRemainingAcceptance: SQLite/Supabase cleanup parity, indexed lookup and paginated catalog.

findings.finding: Open image upload endpoint lets anyone pin arbitrary images under the platform's Pinata account
findings.originalRecommendation: Require a wallet-bound action (for example only accept uploads referenced by a prepare call, or an EIP-191 signed upload intent). Add a global daily upload cap and /64 bucketing. Periodically unpin CIDs that no registered token references. Confirm the Pinata plan's file and storage limits.
findings.implementationAndRemainingAcceptance: Raster validation, content dedup, bounded shared cost and sustained-upload challenge. No per-upload wallet signature.

findings.finding: Weak abuse limits: per-IP limiter is bypassed by IPv6 rotation, a full IP table returns 503 to everyone, and the 32-request concurrency cap is checked before rate limiting
findings.originalRecommendation: Before marketing: set workers_dev:false and add Cloudflare rate-limiting rules on /api/*. In code: bucket IPv6 by /64, use LRU eviction instead of the global 503, apply a per-IP limit and per-IP concurrency cap before the global 32-slot cap (and before draining the body), and add a separate tighter limit for expensive routes (/rpc, first-buy, prepare, token-images).
findings.implementationAndRemainingAcceptance: /64, bounded LRU, source admission before body/global slots, workers_dev false in source. Actual edge setup pending.

findings.finding: All Robinhood API traffic goes to one Durable Object capped at 32 concurrent requests, and each wallet request in a signing flow re-fetches the slow /config endpoint
findings.originalRecommendation: Cache the verified /config result server-side for a few seconds, keyed by block, and cache MusegodReader identity per block. In the client, validate once per signing step rather than once per JSON-RPC request. Load-test the DO before announcing, and consider sharding read-only routes (market, info) away from the signing-critical /config.
findings.disposition: Single DO capacity / slow config — mitigated
findings.implementationAndRemainingAcceptance: One complete check per actual signing; bounded read retry and shared preparation slots. No unmeasured read-sharding architecture added.

findings.finding: Every wallet request triggers a burst of API calls, which collides with the 180 req/min per-IP limit and retryCount:0, so flows can abort or report a confirmed transaction as 'still pending'
findings.originalRecommendation: Validate once per wallet request, skip eth_chainId, and cache /config and RPC chainId for a few seconds within one flow. Batch the LI.FI whitelist reads with multicall. Give the RPC transport bounded retries with backoff for 429/503, and make confirmed() keep waiting through transient poll errors. Raise or separate the rate-limit bucket for /rpc.
findings.disposition: Wallet request amplification / poll failure — implemented
findings.implementationAndRemainingAcceptance: Read-only RPC retry, transient confirmation polling, actual signing-step checks; no broadcast retries.

findings.finding: Quote freshness checks compare server timestamps with the browser clock at zero tolerance, so users whose clock runs a few seconds slow cannot launch or pay with LI.FI
findings.originalRecommendation: Do not compare server stamps to the browser clock with zero tolerance. Either send serverNow in each response and evaluate quotedAt/obtainedAt/expiresAt against a measured client-server offset, or allow a bounded skew (for example ±30 s on 'not in the future') and enforce freshness on the server (/launch/validate, /launch/simulate, the LI.FI re-check) and on-chain (the first-buy deadline already d
findings.implementationAndRemainingAcceptance: Existing windows cannot be renewed by later clock correction.

findings.finding: Uncached LI.FI calls let one anonymous client (or ~34 open Create tabs) use up the shared 100 req/min LI.FI key and block every launch
findings.originalRecommendation: Cache /v1/token prices server-side per (chain, asset) for 30-60 s and merge in-flight requests. Cache or share one opening valuation per asset for a few seconds, and drop the duplicate valuation in preflightFirstBuyPayment (or reuse its result). Add a stricter per-IP limit on LI.FI-backed routes. Confirm or raise the LI.FI key tier. Expose a LI.FI health signal in readiness/monitoring.
findings.implementationAndRemainingAcceptance: Short caches/merge/global quotas/reserved recovery budget; key-tier verification remains external.

findings.finding: No jurisdiction or terms gating, although the app sells and delivers Robinhood stock tokens that may not go to US persons
findings.originalRecommendation: Get a legal decision before real-money launch. At minimum: - Geo-block the US and Robinhood's restricted jurisdictions in the Worker (request.cf.country) for signing-related endpoints (/launch/*, /first-buy/*, /quote, /rpc) and in the UI. - Require an explicit non-US-person attestation and terms acceptance before wallet signing, and link each token's terms(). - Monitor registry isBlocked() for the
findings.implementationAndRemainingAcceptance: Single English issuer/jurisdiction sentence + link; no location gate or checkbox. No legal acceptance conclusion is inferred.

findings.finding: Signing is enabled in production although no real-wallet mainnet launch, first buy, LI.FI conversion, trade or claim has ever been done (no canary)
findings.originalRecommendation: Turn signing off, or allowlist operator wallets, until the operator runs a recorded small-value canary on 4663: 1. One ordinary launch. 2. One guarded first buy paid via a LI.FI ETH/USDG conversion. 3. A buy and a sell. 4. A creator fee claim and a treasury fee claim. 5. Registration and receipt recovery after a reload.  Then enable signing for everyone.
findings.implementationAndRemainingAcceptance: Explicit small-value launch/trade/claim/restore canary and paused compatible release checklist below.

findings.finding: No mainnet signing evidence exists. The WalletProvider signing code is untested, and the browser acceptance test runs on chain 31337 with a stub wallet
findings.originalRecommendation: Before announcing, run a small real-money canary with a team wallet on MetaMask extension and MetaMask Mobile. Cover: launch without a buy, launch with first buy plus approval, LI.FI conversion, Doppler buy and sell, fee claim, MUSEGOD buy and sell, and the network add/switch. Record the transaction hashes. Until then, consider writesEnabled:false or an allowlist.
findings.disposition: No real desktop/mobile wallet proof — pending
findings.implementationAndRemainingAcceptance: Real browser app mock checks cover UI logic; extension/mobile real-wallet mainnet scenarios remain not_run.

findings.finding: Any caller can buy the engine's priced fee assets at the 99% oracle floor through a self-chosen route
findings.originalRecommendation: Accept and document a 1-2% leak, or restrict conversions to a keeper or allow-listed route, and/or tighten the floor using a DEX TWAP check. Use maxAge somewhat above the heartbeat to avoid periodic StaleFeed windows.
findings.implementationAndRemainingAcceptance: Fixed 99% first-stage and 98.5% Swapper offer are explicit; not an end-to-end fee guarantee.

findings.finding: Production fee/buyback path is not live: engine disabled by config; the platform's 'buyback budget' accrues to one EOA with no Robinhood buyback tooling
findings.originalRecommendation: Treat this as a disclosure and ops decision before launch. Either change the /buyback copy to 'discretionary; no automated or batch buyback on Robinhood yet', or ship a fixed, redeployed engine. Prefer a multisig over an EOA for PLATFORM_TREASURY.
findings.disposition: Automated buyback not live — implemented source, pending activation
findings.implementationAndRemainingAcceptance: New graph, Vault and strict one-time canonical proof; no old Engine activation or false live claim.

findings.finding: The 'unpriced' path is custodial and untested: most launch pairs and every meme-token fee go to a 1-of-1-controlled Splits account that the UI calls 'independent'
findings.originalRecommendation: Before activating: change the copy to say the account is operator-controlled. Demonstrate a native automation run with a real meme token. Consider sending unpriced meme-token fees to DEAD or a time-locked contract instead of a 1-of-1 account.
findings.disposition: Unpriced operator custody / native run — partial
findings.implementationAndRemainingAcceptance: Copy identifies operator control; originally priced assets never silently enter it. Actual native scheduled fee-to-burn run pending.

findings.finding: WethForwarder's MAX approval lets anyone push any WETH held by the Splits workspace treasury into the Swapper
findings.originalRecommendation: Use a dedicated source account used only for buybacks, or keep a bounded allowance that the automation tops up.
findings.disposition: Unlimited old Forwarder approval — implemented gate, execution pending
findings.implementationAndRemainingAcceptance: Old allowance must be zero, new allowance finite and at most2.88WETH with exact proof; current source allowance exhaustion or oversizing only pauses forwarding.

findings.finding: Buyback burn-history scan is sized in blocks and covers only about 50 seconds on Robinhood's 100ms blocks
findings.originalRecommendation: Build burn history from the deployment block with a persisted cursor or indexer, or rely on the on-chain cumulative counters (totalDirectBurned, totalConvertedWeth). Size any recent window in seconds, not blocks.
findings.implementationAndRemainingAcceptance: Persistent deployment-start cursor, canonical checkpoints, transfer attribution and catch-up progress.

findings.finding: Buyback oracle staleness cap (86400s) does not fit 24/5 equity feeds: weekly conversion outages and a permanent fee lock if a feed is retired
findings.originalRecommendation: Before activating the fee engine, redeploy the oracle with market-hours-aware staleness: for example, a maxAge of at least 4 days for 24/5 feeds together with the oraclePaused check and a sanity deviation bound. Raise or remove the MAX_FEED_AGE cap.  Also add an engine fallback that routes a configured asset to the automation path after a long, provable staleness period, so retired feeds cannot lo
findings.implementationAndRemainingAcceptance: Expected stale/paused queues plus delayed feed replacement; no permissive four-day extension or custody bypass.

findings.finding: Robinhood stock amounts are shown in raw token units, ignoring the ERC-8056 uiMultiplier (CRWD is already 4.0)
findings.originalRecommendation: For chain 4663, read uiMultiplier() (and any pending newUIMultiplier()/effectiveAt()) and render share equivalents, or label amounts as 'token units'. Correct the protocol.ts comment.
findings.implementationAndRemainingAcceptance: Raw units and known share equivalent; original calldata units preserved.

findings.finding: The app treats issuer-controlled paired assets as plain ERC20s; pause, blocklist and upgrade powers combined with permanently locked liquidity are neither detected nor disclosed
findings.originalRecommendation: - In stocks() and assertStock, read token paused(), registry paused() and isBlocked for the user, PoolManager, guard and treasury. Mark the asset unavailable and block new payments and launches with a clear banner. - Map 0x1309a563 and 0x75e91ce7 to a specific message, and change the test to use the real Robinhood revert data. - Before go-live, disclose in the UI that liquidity is permanently lock
findings.implementationAndRemainingAcceptance: Known transfer pause/full simulation errors stop corresponding operation; missing auxiliary state warns. Identity/pause/reference disclosure retained.

findings.finding: Launches from contract-account wallets (for example ERC-4337 smart accounts) execute on-chain but can never be registered, and nothing warns the user beforehand
findings.originalRecommendation: Before the approval step, check the connected account's code. Block or warn on contract accounts, but allow the 0xef0100 7702 delegation prefix. Alternatively, register from the GuardedLaunch or Create event creator plus calldata equality, rather than from tx.from.
findings.disposition: Unsupported smart account cannot register — implemented prepayment boundary
findings.implementationAndRemainingAcceptance: Unsupported contract creator detected before payment; supported existing account flow unchanged. No new login/connection step.

findings.finding: A payment record whose transaction never mines blocks all launches from that wallet, with no way out in the UI
findings.originalRecommendation: When the original hash has no receipt and the account's latest nonce is greater than the recorded nonce, treat the record as superseded and allow it to be cleared. Also add an explicit 'Discard this pending payment record' action, with a warning, once the original hash has had no receipt for N minutes. Funds can never be lost this way because conversion output is only credited via verify().
findings.implementationAndRemainingAcceptance: Intent-local marker/lock, saved independent drafts and exact replacement recovery; another intent proceeds.

findings.finding: Opening price can be pushed for thin-liquidity pairs such as MUSEGOD; the 5% check only measures the round-trip spread
findings.originalRecommendation: For assets priced by a single AMM pool (MUSEGOD and other OTHERS entries), add an independent check, e.g. require the LI.FI mid to be within X% of the pool's 5-10 min TWAP (the codebase already has a SushiSwap TWAP reader for the retired policy), or remove such assets from lifi-launch-assets.json.
findings.disposition: Thin launch reference price — product decision
findings.implementationAndRemainingAcceptance: Spread/independent reference warnings, no promised fair opening valuation; invalid identity/execution still fails.

findings.finding: The hard-coded LiFiGenericSwapCompleted topic has 2 extra hex characters, so the malformed-event guard never runs

findings.finding: ETH payment for a WETH-paired first buy is routed through LI.FI's 'wrapper' tool and pays a 0.25% LI.FI fee for a plain wrap

findings.implementationAndRemainingAcceptance: Direct deposit quote, exact Deposit receipt, combined approval/launch browser regression.

findings.originalRecommendation: - In assertStock (or prepare, quote and fees), read tokenPaused(), the registry's paused(), and registry.isBlocked() for the creator, PoolManager, router, Permit2 and guard. findings.originalRecommendation: For Robinhood ERC20 stocks, read uiMultiplier(). Show "≈ N shares" next to raw amounts the same way the B20 path does. Fix the misleading comment in protocol.ts, which is true for Base B20 but not for Robinhood.
findings.implementationAndRemainingAcceptance: Observed/scheduled UI multiplier shown as auxiliary information.

findings.finding: Config drift: dead or missing Worker vars, and the fee engine is deployed but not wired or checked by CI

findings.finding: Tests for abuse controls and Worker routing do not exercise the production path
findings.originalRecommendation: Add a workerd-based test (vitest-pool-workers or miniflare) for worker/index.ts covering routing, header overwrite, body limit and concurrency. Add limiter tests with IPv6 and missing-Origin requests. Add LIFI_API_KEY to the bundle secret scan.
findings.disposition: Worker controls only mocked at app layer — implemented

findings.finding: Client clock skew of more than 5 s behind, or 60 s ahead, makes every MUSEGOD quote fail, with a misleading error
findings.originalRecommendation: Measure skew on receipt: local expiry = receivedAt + (expiresAt - quotedAt). Or drop the future-quotedAt check and rely on the on-chain deadline. Show a clear error message about the device clock.
